chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Jacksonville drugstore: trombonist George Washington looks out for him
summary: On the way south George Washington went with him into a Jacksonville drugstore to show him how to behave, as Clarke bought toiletries.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, when we went to Jacksonville -- now this is strange. Now, George Washington, the trombone player, well, they all knew that I had never been south. So we kind of stopped -- we were in Jacksonville, so we kind of stopped --
This was on the way down?

Yeah, on the way down. We stopped by a drug store, you know, and the bus stops, and there's a colored restaurant. So I said, 'George, I'm going to get some Iodent toothpaste,' -- tooth powder at that time. And I remember very well. A toothbrush, some talcum powder and a bar of soap I needed. So George says, 'I better go with you, because I'll show you how to act, because I don't want you to get

in no trouble." This is my first experience. So I get out of the bus with George in front of me. "Now, wait a minute. Wait a minute. I'm going to show you how to do it. I don't want you to get in any trouble." I said okay. So we go into the drug store. So George, at the counter, is like the door is here and the counter is like this, you know, and the owner's behind the counter this way, so I'm in front of the counter this way. So the toothpaste and things I wanted are here. So I walk over and said, "I'd like a can of Iodent tooth powder." And he said, "Why certainly." "And a nice toothbrush, not too stiff, kind of medium." So he gave me the tooth paste, a tooth brush, and I said, "A bar of --," what was it, Camay, or -- no, Lifebuoy. That's what it was. "And a bar of Lifebuoy soap." He said, "Will that be all, sir?" I said, "No, I'd like some talcum." We didn't have deodorant in those times, and I used to just put talcum under my arms, you know. I said, "No, I'll have a box of talcum powder. What's that nice smelling powder? It smells a little like rose, you know." He says, "Oh, yeah. I know." So he reached up and got the one I wanted to. I forget the name of it. He wrapped it up and said, "Will that be all, sir?" I said, "That'll about wrap it up." Now George is standing at the door, you know, and I've always worn a tam. I found it so practical.
